archetype.name: Playoff Team (three-point offense)
archetype.definition: A Boston side with five straight winning seasons behind it that still plays the same slow, three-heavy, low-turnover style, but now has to prove it can defend and rebound at its old level with a thin backcourt.

report.headline: The shooting travels, the glass doesn't: two games, one real question
report.take:
Two games is almost nothing, but the shape of this Boston team is already familiar. It plays slow (a Pace of 95.1 against a league 101.4), takes a huge share of its shots from three (3PA Rate 46.3, 4th), barely turns it over (TOV % 11.6, 3rd) and almost never gets to the line (FT Rate 21.1, 28th). Every one of those habits matches the 2021-22 through 2025-26 teams, which won between 51 and 64 games. The offense sits at a 115.7 ORtg, 10th, carried by 39.5% shooting from three. That is a sound base, not a hot streak.

The split from the past is on the other end. A franchise that finished no worse than 5th in Def Rank across those five seasons opens at 21st, with a 117.8 DRtg. Some of that is noise: opponents have made 38.8% of their threes (26th), while Boston has held up well where defense is more repeatable, with Opp Rim FG % at 62.2 (9th) and Opp Rim Rate at 27.1 (8th). The part that looks more structural is the boards. DRB % of 67.5 ranks 27th, a long way from the 75.7 of last season, and RPG of 38 is 29th.

The roster explains the site's 22nd-place ranking better than the record does. Paul George has been the best player on the floor: 53 points on a 67.1 TS %, a 7.5 BPM and a +29.1 On-Off, good for 1st on the power-forward tab. Jayson Tatum has used the most possessions (USG % 32.9) but shot poorly, a 47.4 TS %. The guards are the real worry. The Backcourt grade is an F, Payton Pritchard sits at a -7.1 BPM, and Derrick White has a -11.2 On-Off despite efficient scoring. Two forwards are carrying a team whose guard play hasn't held up.

The differential is -4 and the margin implies exactly the one win Boston has, so there is no luck to strip out yet. The 41-win pace the sheet shows is a two-game artifact. The history and the shooting profile point higher, provided the defensive rebounding recovers.

strengths.title: Three-point volume with real accuracy
strengths.body: Boston takes threes at the 4th-highest rate and makes them at 39.5%, 6th in the league. The volume is a long-running identity (3PA Rate was 46.7 last season), so the approach will last. The accuracy will probably cool toward the 36-37% range of recent years, which still supports a top-10 offense.

strengths.title: Ball security wins possessions back
strengths.body: A TOV % of 11.6 ranks 3rd, and the defense is forcing turnovers at 15.6 (8th). In a slow game, that steady possession edge is a big part of how Boston beats teams. The ball-security half has held for years: TOV % was 11.2 last season.

strengths.title: Paul George as the engine
strengths.body: George has scored 53 points on a 67.1 TS % and posts a 7.5 BPM with a +29.1 On-Off. Those are by far the best impact numbers on the roster, and they explain why the frontcourt grades a B- while the guards grade an F. His efficiency will drift down, but he is clearly the hub right now.

concerns.title: Defensive glass has collapsed
concerns.body: Boston has grabbed only 67.5% of opponents' misses, 27th, after 75.7% last season. Second chances are a big reason the DRtg sits at 117.8 even though the rim defense has been fine. This is the number to watch: two games can produce it by accident, but it is the clearest break from the franchise's recent identity.

concerns.title: Backcourt grades out at F
concerns.body: White and Pritchard play the most guard minutes. Pritchard's -7.1 BPM and White's -11.2 On-Off say the units around them have been beaten. Behind them, Baylor Scheierman and Hugo González have struggled in short minutes. If the guard group doesn't improve, George and Tatum have to create nearly everything, and Tatum's 47.4 TS % shows the strain.

concerns.title: No free throws to fall back on
concerns.body: An FT Rate of 21.1, 28th, means Boston's offense lives and dies with the jumper. This is not new (it was 20.7 last season), but it leaves less margin on cold shooting nights.

trend.note: A loss at Detroit and then a four-point home win over New York. Two games give no slope, only a baseline that looks like a softer-defending version of recent Boston teams.

weekAhead.headline: Three home games against weak teams, then a Houston test
weekAhead.body:
The first four games are the softest stretch Boston is likely to see for a while. There are three straight at home against Chicago (25th on the site, Net Rtg -12.4) and Brooklyn (26th, winless), then a trip to Orlando, whose offense ranks 26th. Chicago has the worst eFG % in the league at 46.0 and the worst 3P % at 22.6, and Brooklyn's defense allows an Opp eFG % of 60.7 (29th). A shooting team with few turnovers should be able to win those games on efficiency. Both weeks' pairs of games come on back-to-back nights, which tests a thin guard rotation.

The finale at Houston is a different matter. The Rockets are 3-0, 5th on the site, with a 122.9 ORtg (3rd) and A+ grades for both wings and frontcourt. Their defense has held opponents to 29.3% from three, 5th, which goes straight at Boston's main weapon. Winning the first four would make the week a success; Houston measures how far this team is from the top.

keyMatchups.title: Boston's boards against Chicago's misses
keyMatchups.body: Chicago shoots terribly but rebounds well (RPG 48.3, 7th) and lives at the line (FT Rate 38.8, 3rd). That pressure lands on Boston's two weakest areas, defensive rebounding and free-throw volume. If the Bulls stay close in either home game, it will be through second chances and free throws.

keyMatchups.title: Brooklyn's leaky perimeter defense
keyMatchups.body: The Nets allow 40.3% from three (27th) and a 60.7 Opp eFG %. Power forwards and centers have done damage against them, with PF and C each taking a larger share of points than the league norm. That sets up well for George and Hauser stretching the floor from the four.

keyMatchups.title: Houston shutting down power forwards
keyMatchups.body: Houston has allowed opposing power forwards just 5.33 points a game, 2nd-fewest, and only 4.8% of the points it allows. Boston's scoring runs through its PFs, George and Tatum. If that holds, Boston needs its guards to produce, which they haven't yet.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Boston's DRB % climbs back toward last season's level against a Chicago team that crashes the offensive glass.

restOfSeason.body:
The offensive style is durable: it matches five seasons of history, so a top-10 offense is the reasonable expectation even after the 39.5% three-point shooting cools. The defense should improve from 21st simply because opponents won't keep shooting 38.8% from three. Boston's rim numbers already look like a good defense's. The open question is the defensive rebounding and a backcourt graded F. If those stay where they are, this is a mid-40s-win team that relies on George; if the glass returns to normal, it moves back toward the top of the East.

The 41-win pace is two games of noise. A projection of roughly 45 to 53 wins weighs the history and the shooting against a roster that looks thinner than the 56-win group of last season.
swingFactors: Defensive rebounding returning to recent levels
Guard play lifting the backcourt grade
Tatum's efficiency catching up to his usage

confidence.note: Two games played; history and style carry more weight than the current numbers.
